subject.title: Bug: preflight (budget-triggered) compaction hard-capped at ~60s, ignores compaction.timeoutSeconds

question: Should the canonical fix for this issue be the filtered preflight cancellation contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590, or should maintainers require a different timeout/config-gate path first?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior boundary is maintainer-owned because required preflight compaction must ignore lifecycle timeouts without losing explicit stop/restart cancellation, and the alternative config gate adds new public configuration surface.

options.title: Accept the filtered-signal PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 as the canonical cancellation fix after normal review and proof refresh, leaving the config gate out of the bug fix.

options.title: Require exact slow-backend proof first
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until a redacted vLLM/Qwen-style or equivalent slow-backend proof shows the 60-second lifecycle timeout no longer wins.

options.title: Split a config-gate follow-up
options.body: Land the cancellation fix first and open a separate product discussion only if maintainers still want a `compaction.preflight.enabled` escape hatch.

recommendation.title: Accept the filtered-signal PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 as the canonical cancellation fix after normal review and proof refresh, leaving the config gate out of the bug fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is mainly about reply cancellation semantics, and this history trail ties that contract to prior reply lifecycle work.
